readmeHtml:
WandEnhancer

Warning

DMCA notice. On 2026-11-10 GitHub received a DMCA takedown notice for several files of this repository. The files named in the notice were removed from the repository and its history, so the project does not build from this repository at the moment.

An open-source tool that extends the local client-side configuration of the Wand app and improves its UX.

This project has no official downloads and no official video tutorials. GitHub releases contain notes only, never .exe files. Scammers use the project's name for fake tutorials and put malware or password stealers in the video descriptions. An executable or archive from a video, a website or a mirror did not come from this project, and we are not responsible for it. The only official source is this repository. Look-alike forks and accounts are not ours.

Network and privacy

The patcher modifies files in the selected local Wand installation. By default it has no update check and no telemetry. Wand itself stays an online application. The optional remote web panel starts a LAN HTTP/WebSocket server and uses Wand API and CDN data, such as trainer translations and artwork.

FAQ

Why is there no .exe in GitHub Releases? Unsigned and self-built patching tools were repeatedly reuploaded, mislabeled and flagged by third-party scanners, so the project stopped distributing prebuilt executables. Releases are notes-only on purpose.

Can I use a binary built by someone else? Treat it as untrusted. This repository cannot verify or support third-party builds.

Screenshots

License

Apache-2.0, see LICENSE.

Support

If you find this project useful, you can support its development with any option below.

Legal disclaimer: This project is a third-party enhancement tool intended solely for educational, research and local interoperability purposes. It does not distribute any proprietary code or bypass server-side validations. All modifications are performed locally to customize the user's interface.

releases.body:
### Features

- The patch dialog now remembers your last choices (patches, method, auto-apply, custom scripts), and the main window remembers the Wand install. By @w0wzahh in #387.
- A Re-detect button next to the install path rescans the current install after a Wand update, without restarting the app. By @w0wzahh in #387.
- A Copy diagnostics button next to the log copies the enhancer version, OS, install path, Wand version and patch state, ready to paste into a bug report. By @w0wzahh in #387.

### Fixes

- Fixed the patcher targeting an old Wand version after an update. The latest install was chosen by the folder's modification time, which a virus scan or the enhancer's own backup can bump on the previous version. It is now chosen by the version in the folder name. By @w0wzahh in #383. #374
- Restore now removes the deployed `WandEnhancerWatcher.exe`, and a file that is still locked is skipped with a warning instead of failing the Restore. By @w0wzahh in #386.
- The log now warns when a newer Wand version sits next to the selected one. By @w0wzahh in #386. #374
- Fixed the web tests failing on a source ZIP download, which stopped the build at "Test web-panel". #384

### Features

- Drag the Wand folder or `Wand.exe` onto the window to pick the install when it is not detected.
- Bengali (Bangladesh) language by @amiMohammad in #305.
- The remote panel gives a short haptic tap on toggles, action buttons and steppers. It works in Android browsers only, iOS Safari has no Vibration API.

### Fixes

- Fixed Patch and Restore failing on files still locked by Wand helpers. Helpers such as Squirrel's `Update.exe`, crashpad and the deployed watcher are now closed by executable path, file operations retry while a lock clears, and a lock that stays names the process holding it. By @w0wzahh in #359. #181 #326
- Fixed the build failing when the checkout path contains `&`. By @w0wzahh in #359.
- Fixed a failed restore of the original files leaving `app.asar.unpacked` half empty and Wand unable to start. That step is now rolled back with the rest of the patch.
- Fixed sharing violations while neutralizing the integrity check: the auxiliary service is now closed before Patch and Restore. Also fixed the missing `netstandard` reference in the build. By @LastRq in #301.
- A patch now fails and rolls back if the auxiliary service disappears while patch

### Fixes

- Fixed trainers failing to start after enhancing on Wand 12.61.0 and newer: the auxiliary service rejected trainer injection with `InjectDll: Client integrity check failed`, which Wand shows as "We're having trouble loading the mods into your game". Fixed by @RatedRCustomer in #345. #311 #320 #334 #343 #347 #354
- Fixed auto-apply after update, which never actually fired: Squirrel rewrites the root execution stub while applying the update, erasing the deployed launcher before it could run. A background update watcher by @Glitxhhh from #318 now re-applies the saved patch selection the moment a new Wand version lands, starts with Windows, and stops on Restore.

### Features

- **New fixed static patch method, now the default.** It applies the patch on disk, which is more stable for most users than the runtime approach - so it is the default now. A *Patch method* selector at the top of the patch dialog switches between it and the in-memory *Supervised* method, with an info note on the trade-off.
- The deployed launcher now wears Wand's own icon, so replaced shortcuts look unchanged.

### Improvements

- *Auto-apply after updates* is off by default.

### Important

- The bundled `version.dll` proxy is gone. The launcher now starts Wand and keeps the patch applied in every process Electron spawns, for as long as Wand runs. This is what fixes Wand refusing to launch after enhancing on related issues: #207 #210 #211 #213 #214 #217
- The native helper and its CMake build step were removed. Building from source no longer needs `CMake` or the Visual Studio C++ workload.
- WandEnhancer now installs itself as the Wand launcher entry point, so starting Wand goes through the patcher. Restoring a backup puts the original launcher back.

### Features

- **Auto-patch after Wand updates.** Enable *Auto-apply after updates* in the patch dialog and your selection is saved next to the launcher. When Wand updates and drops the patches, the next launch re-applies them. On failure the UI opens and shows which patch broke instead of silently starting an unpatched client.
- **Rewritten patch engine with legacy version support.** Patches are located structurally instead of by regex signature: each anchors on something Wand does not rename between builds. A client rebuild that only re-minifies no longer breaks patching, and older clients keep

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source .NET patcher for Wand that enhances UI layouts, adds AI features, and enables remote model inference.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: WandEnhancer is a local interoperability tool designed to modify and extend the Wand application client. It works by applying a .NET patcher to local installation files and injecting a proxy `version.dll` that modifies Electron's ASAR-integrity fuse byte within the Wand process itself. This allows users to unlock advanced client-side theme customizations, integrate new AI features, and manage local environment configurations without connecting to external telemetry services. Additionally, it spins up a local LAN HTTP/WebSocket server to host a Remote Web Panel, allowing users to control their active Wand session directly from a mobile device.
keyFeatures: Electron ASAR Patching: Uses a bundled `version.dll` proxy to safely bypass ASAR integrity checks directly within the Wand process.
Local Environment Management: Automatically handles compatibility adjustments and local configuration settings for new Wand client versions.
Remote Web Panel: Hosts a local HTTP/WebSocket server on port 3223, enabling smartphone remote control via LAN or VPNs like Tailscale.
Client-Side Customization: Unlocks advanced UI layout adjustments and custom theming options that are otherwise restricted.
AI toolset integration: Enhances the core Wand experience by exposing hidden or modified AI-driven toolsets.

useCases.title: Mobile Remote Control
useCases.description: Scanning a QR code to control the desktop Wand application from a smartphone while on the same Wi-Fi network.

useCases.title: UI Customization
useCases.description: Applying custom themes and layout modifications to the Wand client by bypassing its default ASAR integrity fuse.

useCases.title: Secure Client Patching
useCases.description: Modifying local Wand application files without triggering external telemetry or update services, ensuring privacy.

useCases.title: Continuous Compatibility
useCases.description: Automatically updating configuration settings to maintain patch compatibility whenever the Wand application receives an update.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Wand Enhancer targets users of the Wand application seeking improved UX and extended local client-side configurations. It is an open-source interoperability tool.
